A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Mixture-of-Graphs (MoG) work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support comparison across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original graph-learning experiments, sparsification comparisons, inference measurements and sensitivity analyses in Section 4 and Appendix G.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds expert-count sensitivity, timing and router-noise results in Tables 13–15.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the routing mechanism, four pruning criteria, graph mixture, post-sparsification and training loss. Appendix C revises the mathematical derivation without documenting a changed operational procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six datasets: OGBN-ARXIV, OGBN-PROTEINS, OGBN-PRODUCTS, OGBG-PPA, MNIST and CIFAR-10. The added analyses use retained node-classification tasks and datasets.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding benchmark and efficiency tables. The updated ICPG citation refers to the same comparator; the new noise controls are MoG ablations.

E3.justification: v2 adds expert-count sweeps on OGBN-PROTEINS+RevGNN and timing measurements on OGBN-ARXIV+GraphSAGE, plus Gaussian, zero and fixed-0.2 router-noise controls. Table 15 specifies k=3 for its ablation. Existing benchmark splits, metrics and stated default settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices G.2–G.3 extend the existing expert-count analysis with RevGNN accuracy and GraphSAGE timing measurements, and add a router-noise ablation. These are focused diagnostic additions. The earlier total-expert efficiency analysis is retained in Section 4.5 rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Existing five-run statements and mean/standard-deviation reporting are retained. New Tables 13–15 report point values without introducing additional run counts, seeds, uncertainty estimates or significance tests.

E6.justification: Previously reported benchmark and efficiency values are retained. New Table 13 reports a RevGNN peak of 89.09 at k=3; Table 14 adds timing results. At 50% sparsity, Table 15 reports test accuracies of 69.06, 67.05 and 68.45 for Gaussian, zero and fixed noise, respectively. These are supplementary results, not improvements over v1 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: Appendix C replaces v1's directly asserted closed-form expression in Equation (26) with a trace derivation in v2 Equations (26)–(29). Its final expression changes U^T U to the expert-specific projector U_m U_m^T. This local mathematical revision is not reconciled with the retained formula in Section 3 and Algorithm 1.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims of locally customized sparsification, Grassmann-based graph combination, inference acceleration and performance enhancement. The headline quantitative claims and contribution scope are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations that selecting two or three experts balances performance and runtime, and that stochastic router noise benefits performance. The existing efficiency interpretation is relocated, while the limitation concerning unexplored multi-hop contexts remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Tables 14–15 add computational-cost measurements by selected-expert count and explicit settings for the noise ablation. Appendix F's implementation details, hardware and access links are retained. Changing the description of the same code URL from publicly to anonymously available does not establish changed access.

R1.justification: v2 removes Roller et al.'s Hash layers for large sparse models from the MoE discussion and bibliography. Research positioning otherwise remains stable; author-year formatting and the ICPG publication update do not introduce new related work.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited prose edits, expands the sensitivity-analysis introduction and adds Section 4.5 by combining relocated efficiency discussion with an ablation summary. Author information, citation style and bibliography ordering change, but most narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 13–15 and relocates/reformats v1 Table 12 as main-text Table 5. Title styling, running headers, table widths and float placements change. Figures 1–4 retain their graphics and content.

improvement.justification: Tables 13–15 provide useful additional evidence about expert selection, runtime and router noise, strengthening the assessment of design choices beyond v1. Moving efficiency evidence into Section 4.5 also improves accessibility. The gain is limited by inconsistencies: the revised Appendix C formula disagrees with the retained main algorithm, and Table 15's k=3 conflicts with the statement that all experiments use k=2.
